newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait bourse trade booms, index hits record.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait bourse trade booms, index hits record.

text.p: Kuwait's share index ended an active week on Wednesday at a record high despite growing anxiety in the Gulf region over a new possible U.S.-Iraqi military clash.
The index rose 35.1 points or 2.1 percent over the week to 1,671.8.
Daily average volume rose 51.6 percent to 210 million shares, with total volume of 1.05 billion shares. The exchange operates for two-and-a-half hours a day from Saturday to Wednesday.
Traded value gained 64.9 percent on a daily average basis to 41.4 million dinars ($138.4 million), with a total value of 207.2 dinars. Deals rose 45.4 percent to an average of 2,125 a day.
Gainers led losers 31-7, with 17 stocks unchanged.

Exchange Director-General Hisham al-Oteibi told Reuters the market was booming for several reasons, including renewed U.S. commitment for Kuwait's security, progress in settling a $5.5 billion sovereign loan and private sector bad debts in addition to strong mid-year results by most listed companies.
Sentiment about the economy had been boosted by the scheduled conclusion in December of repayments of principal on the jumbo loan by the Kuwaiti government.

Also most debtors owing billions of dinars met a September 6 deadline to pay millions as part of a plan to settle long-standing debts with an original value of $20 billion. The debt is owed by businessmen and private companies including listed firms.

The United States this month fired 44 cruise missiles at Iraqi targets in southern Iraq, north of Kuwait, in retaliation for Baghdad's involvement in Kurdish factional fighting in the north of the country. Kuwaitis saw the move as a strong U.S. commitment to the oil state's security against former occupier Iraq.

Other positive factors included recent government predictions of a large cut in the state budget deficit and the country's political stability, Oteibi said. "People feel confident in the political stability of Kuwait," he said.
The end of the summer holidays was another factor, dealers said, noting that talk of privatisation plans stimulated the market.
After the 1991 Gulf War the government announced plans to shed its stake at about 60 firms and at a later stage in state-run services such as electricity and water.
Privatisation operations traditionally increase activity in the market.
The most active stocks were Commercial Bank, Burgan Bank, Investment Projects, Coast Development, United Realty, Pearl of Kuwait Real Estate and Kuwait Real Estate.
Banks were the most active sector by value with 41.9 percent, followed by investment shares with 24.7 percent and property companies with 21.6 percent.
Investments were the most active by volume with 33.6 percent. Banks came second with 28.6 percent and property firms third with 26.8 percent.
